_authored: authored by Fidelity Wave C, 2026-09-09. Factual audit only: NO runtime geometry was changed by this file's mission. Not generated by a tool; edit deliberately.
what: The Northeastern front quadrangle, measured: what Krentzman actually is, what the runtime has instead, which of the enclosing buildings have quad-facing entrances, why Ell and Curry still cannot be separated, and which un-modelled buildings actually contribute screen area.
attribution: City of Boston Open Data, Boston Buildings with Roof Breaks - PDDL (odc-pddl). The enclosing footprints and every derived boundary point below come from this layer.
OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 - used ONLY for the 3,345 m2 area figure as a corroborating FACT. No OSM geometry is imported, here or into src/.

Northeastern University ArcGIS Online - audit reference only, per docs/neu/SOURCES.md: 'Absence of a stated restriction is not a grant.' Used for WHICH buildings have accessible entrances and for two official footprint areas. No coordinate from it is copied into src/.

runtime.form: regular octagon, area-derived about the recorded centre

factual.note: The area is the only thing taken from OSM. It is a scalar fact used to CHECK a PDDL-derived shape, not geometry.

errorToday.shapeError: The runtime octagon is REGULAR and closed on all eight sides. The real space is enclosed on three sides and open across a 100 degree sector toward Huntington. That is the error that matters at eye level: a closed symmetric ring reads as a roundabout of grass, not a quadrangle.

derivedForm.method: ray cast from the recorded centre every 10 degrees against the PDDL roof-break faces within 45 m, boundary set 1.2 m off the face; contiguous gaps are left as straight chords between the flanking faces.
derivedForm.principalOpening: bearings 160-250, 100 degrees, flanked by Dodge Hall and Richards Hall - this is the Huntington side, and the canonical spawn sits at bearing 219.8 from the quad centre, in the middle of it

bracket.reading: The truth is bracketed. The runtime is 23% too small; sweeping the open side all the way to the footway is 26% too large. The chord construction lands 5% under, which is the closest of the four and the only one with the right topology.

whyNotApplied: Wave C ran under the brief's own resource gate: swap 83-91% for the whole mission, load averages 8-59, two users on the machine. The brief says perform factual/source analysis only and do not claim visual acceptance from an unreliable host.
This change is visible in the FIRST FRAME of the game, so shipping it without a trustworthy look at it is the one thing the gate exists to prevent.
runtimeRisksToClearFirst: NeuHero._campusGround cuts the park ring as a hole only if EVERY ring vertex lies inside the dilated campus contour (holes = cand.filter(r => r.every(...pointInRing...))). The derived ring reaches 40.3 m where the octagon reached 30.1 m. If one vertex falls outside the contour the hole is dropped silently and the campus ground double-surfaces the whole quadrangle - z-fighting across the entire opening frame. Test this before anything else.

The canonical spawn (-1883, 1677) is 28.3 m from the centre and falls OUTSIDE the derived ring, because the 100 degree chord cuts inside the octagon's 30.1 m radius. It therefore moves from Districts park grass to the NeuHero campus ground surface. Both are real surfaces so it should not be bare terrain, but it is a first-frame material change and must be looked at. Do NOT move the spawn to suit the ring: OPENING_PLAYER is frozen.

Consumers of the ring: Districts (grass), ParkPaths (circulation), Props (planting), Vegetation (understorey 0.06), NeuHero (ground hole), and isReserved/inPark (no-build). The octagon is convex; the derived ring is not. Any consumer assuming convexity has to be checked.

entrances.question: Which opening-facing entrances can be evidenced for the buildings that enclose the quadrangle?
entrances.method: For each of the 82 official accessible-entrance points, the bearing from its building footprint centroid to the entrance was compared with the bearing from that same centroid to the quad centre. A delta under 55 degrees is quad-facing.

findings.Richards Hall: NO accessible entrance anywhere in the 82-point layer. Richards is the 1937-38 first building on the quadrangle; the absence is consistent with a historic building and is a fact about the accessible layer, not proof there is no door.
findings.Ell Hall: two entrances, delta 127.9 and 114.6 degrees - both face AWAY from the quad
findings.Dodge Hall: one entrance, delta 63.9 degrees; it is on the 2.9 degree north face while the quad lies at 299 degrees - faces AWAY
findings.Hayden Hall: delta 5.4 degrees - quad-facing, 55.2 m from the quad centre
findings.Mugar Life Sciences Building: delta 16.4 degrees - quad-facing, 51.9 m from the quad centre

entrances.conclusion: ZERO quad-facing accessible entrances on the three buildings that actually enclose the quadrangle. Hayden and Mugar do have quad-facing entrances but they enclose the room at 1 of 180 rays each - they face its direction from outside it.
entrances.refines: docs/neu/NeuHero.js says the layer 'places NONE of its 82 points on the Krentzman quadrangle frontage'. That is very nearly right and slightly too strong: none on the ENCLOSING buildings, but Hayden and Mugar do face the quad.
entrances.implicationForPhase7: There is no evidence basis for ceremonial portal architecture on the quad frontage of Richards, Ell or Dodge, and the licence ruling forbids copying the entrance coordinates into src/ in any case. The existing modest PDDL-walk-derived doorway cues - a recess, a darker opening, a threshold, a taller head - are the correct level of claim. Upgrading them to porticoes on the quad frontage would be fabricating architecture the evidence argues against.

ellCurry.defect: Ell Hall and Curry Student Center are one mass in the runtime, resolved to Ell by the earliest-year rule. Wave A did not close it and Wave C cannot either.

sourceTruth.reading: The two official footprints sum to the single PDDL part within 2.8%. The PDDL part IS Ell plus Curry, as one physical structure - which is what they are on the ground. The roof-break layer contains no break between them.

splitSearch.method: scanline width and lobe count across the 95-vertex polygon on six axes, looking for a waist a split could honestly follow
splitSearch.result: No axis yields a neck. The polygon is a single lobe at essentially every cross-section and the narrowest INTERIOR widths are 23-95 m. The cut that would reproduce Ell official 2,864 m2 lands where the mass is 44.7 m wide and one continuous lobe - straight through a solid plate.

otherSourcesTried.northeasternArcGIS: DOES separate them, and is the origin of the two official areas. Ruled audit-reference-only by docs/neu/SOURCES.md, which states that hand-copying its coordinates "would be the same act with worse provenance". Not used.
otherSourcesTried.massGisParcels: UNREACHABLE from this environment - services1.arcgis.com is network-blocked here. Worth one attempt from a host that can reach it; both buildings are likely one institutional parcel.

ellCurry.verdict: BLOCKER STANDS. No licence-clean source can support a defensible split line, so none was invented. The merged mass is left exactly as it was.

screenSpaceMitigation.finding: The quad centre projects to s = -83.6 on the mass principal axis, whose own span is -53.7 to +77.2 - the quadrangle lies entirely off the low-s tip. On the official-area reckoning Ell occupies s -53.7 to +16, i.e. the whole quad-facing end.
screenSpaceMitigation.consequence: The Wave-A historic grey-brick treatment currently applied to the merged mass is CORRECT on every surface the quadrangle and the canonical opening can see. The mislabelling is confined to the far north-east end, which no existing gameplay view reaches.
screenSpaceMitigation.priority: LOW for the opening; real for future Centennial-side views. This is a correctness debt, not an opening-frame defect.

waveDPreRank.what: A PRE-rank of un-modelled buildings within 320 m of the canonical opening, by unoccluded projected solid angle from three gameplay viewpoints. This is a shortlist, not a rank.
waveDPreRank.missingTerm: OCCLUSION. Every figure here is an upper bound. The Hurtig precedent is binding: it was picked at 8 degrees off the view axis, built, and then measured at 42 of 42 sample points inside the frustum and ZERO unoccluded. Bearing and solid angle alone have a 0-for-1 record on this campus.
waveDPreRank.gateForWaveD: Before building any of these, run the frustum-plus-raycast test that was used on Hurtig and on the railway, from the canonical opening and from a short natural walk. Build only what survives occlusion.
waveDPreRank.correctionToTheStandingCandidateList: The standing list in CURRENT_VS_REAL.md names Snell Library as the largest missing footprint nearby, and Robinson (13 deg) and Cullinane (17 deg) as near-axis. Measured: Snell Library ranks 12th here and falls in NONE of the three frusta at 220 m; Churchill is likewise in none. The strongest candidates are instead 337 and 335A Huntington Avenue at 51-58 m, East Village (60 m tall, and the only tall thing in the opening frustum), Speare Hall, Marino, and the four HERO_A St. Stephen Street houses at 88-100 m.
